scope: Theorem 7.5 (Filled solver and normalized end) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-with-charge-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 84ca5bc05bc907a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the choices in Section 5, Lemma 6.2, and Proposition 6.6, every sufficiently large N admits a smooth solution (f, Z) of Equation 5.30 on the complete filled manifold ΩN . It satisfies −ϵ < t ≤ Z ≤ PN , ℓ ≤ l ≤ e, |f| + |df| ≤ exp(PN ). The height estimates of Lemma 6.1 also hold. On the physical end, for each fixed integer j ≥ 0 there are cj, Cj > 0, allowed to depend on N, such that f = Oj(e−cjr ), t, Z = Oj(r−1 ), ∆gt = O(r−3−β ). (7.23) In particular both end constants are zero. The solution is obtained by exhausting the outer Dirichlet radius with N fixed. For the resulting solution uΞ is absolutely integrable, u → 1, and the penalty vanishes sufficiently far out on the end.
